items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: I used to listen to that banjo player like John Morrell, he was very popular and good.

ctx.x: How would they, how would the banjo play on that? Was it straight 4-4 or what'd you do like?

Well, it was, well, I can learn it then, I mean, I first started out playing straight 4-4, and after a while I used to listen to that banjo player like John Morrell, he was very popular and good. And the other ones, that boy named Pley, a little blackie, Santiago. Santiago. His uncle played a very nice banjo. I remember he was playing at a place called Eli Beans that was running that place then. When I was young, I used to stand on the outside and listen at him, you see. That's how I developed ideas about…
And, uh, that was, uh, most of the numbers you would play, like Tiger, Egg, and Bucket, uh.
